source_title: The Wheel of Time — Season 1 Episode 1 opening witness
continuity_scope: Amazon/Prime Video television continuity only, restricted to the official Prime Video Season 1 Episode 1 listing and synopsis for “Leavetaking,” with Amazon official series material used solely to identify the opening named cohort and the show’s own Aes Sedai/Warder/One Power framing. The witness concerns a strange noblewoman's arrival in a remote mountain village, her claim about one of five youths and an ancient reincarnated power, and the opening group’s Two Rivers context. Robert Jordan/Brandon Sanderson novels, games, later episodes/seasons, and book-derived identities are excluded.
work_or_witnesses: The Wheel of Time, Prime Video television series, Season 1 Episode 1: “Leavetaking”
Prime Video official Season 1 listing and episode-one synopsis
Amazon official series materials identifying the opening cohort and source-specific role/cosmology terms
coverage_rule: Include the named individual opening cohort identified in the selected official materials: Moiraine Damodred, al’Lan Mandragoran, Rand al’Thor, Egwene al’Vere, Perrin Aybara, Nynaeve al’Meara, and Matrim Cauthon. Peoples, Aes Sedai/Warder roles, the One Power, Two Rivers, the Dragon Reborn, the Dark One, prophecy, institutions, artifacts, and cosmology remain terms or dimensions rather than peer character nodes. All other names, including ones only found in later episodes/seasons, are excluded.
omissions: Every named individual outside the declared seven-person opening cohort, including any only named in later episodes/seasons, broader credits, promotion, books, games, or companion materials.
Robert Jordan/Brandon Sanderson novel continuity, games, later television episodes/seasons, book-derived identities, ranks, family histories, powers, relationships, events, and outcomes.

Exact ages, youth status beyond the official collective wording, gender identity, sexuality, race/ethnicity/cultural coding, disability, trauma, violence/death details, medical claims, institutional law, artifacts, and adaptation-change judgments not directly stated in this bounded witness.

Any answer to which member of the five is the prophesied figure, any later identity reveal, and any claim that an official series summary’s broad world description settles an individual’s specific ability or destiny.
Fan wikis, Wikipedia, databases, non-official recaps, social posts, unlicensed transcripts, and adaptation-comparison commentary.
uncertainties: Prime Video's episode-one synopsis calls one of five youths a reincarnation of an ancient power, but does not name the individual. This pass does not identify a candidate or apply a later reveal.

Amazon describes the first season as Moiraine's journey with five friends from the Two Rivers, identifying their names. It does not provide episode-one, person-by-person age, family, power, sexuality, race/ethnicity, disability, or outcome data; none is inferred.

Amazon’s explanatory material describes Aes Sedai and the One Power in gendered terms. Those descriptions are retained as source-specific fictional framing and do not establish real-world gender categories, essentialist claims about people, or a complete rule system.

Moiraine’s Aes Sedai role and Lan’s Warder connection are official series-material descriptors. They do not authorize importing novel mechanics, later television developments, romance, or unstated bond effects into the episode-one record.

The show is adapted from novels, but adaptation status does not establish equivalence. Any difference between the television program and a book is outside this source pass unless the official television witness itself states it.
evidence_basis: Official Prime Video and Amazon materials only. The Prime Video listing supplies the exact episode-one premise, title, and date. Amazon's official series pages identify the named opening cohort, their Two Rivers/journey context, and the show's source-native Aes Sedai, Warder, One Power, prophecy, and Dark One vocabulary. Later-plot sentences on those pages are expressly excluded.
